title: Exact coordinate Koszul sequence of projective twists
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $n\geq0$, $X=\operatorname{Proj}(A[x_0,\ldots,x_n])$, and $a\in\mathbf Z$. Use the invertible twists $\mathcal O_X(d)$ of [def-pc-projective-space-twist] in the abelian category of $\mathcal O_X$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. There is an exact complex of vector bundles
$$0\longrightarrow\mathcal O_X(a)\longrightarrow\mathcal O_X(a+1)^{\oplus\binom{n+1}{1}}\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow\mathcal O_X(a+i)^{\oplus\binom{n+1}{i}}\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow\mathcal O_X(a+n+1)\longrightarrow0.$$
Its maps are the signed coordinate Koszul maps, defined as follows. For $d\in\mathbf Z$ and $0\leq j\leq n$, let $x_j:\mathcal O_X(d)\to\mathcal O_X(d+1)$ be the $\mathcal O_X$-linear map given on $U_k=D_+(x_k)$ by $e_k^{(d)}\mapsto(x_j/x_k)\,e_k^{(d+1)}$ (these local maps agree on overlaps by the transition rule). Index the summands of $\mathcal O_X(a+i)^{\oplus\binom{n+1}{i}}$ by the subsets $I\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n\}$ with $|I|=i$, the summand of $I$ being a copy $\mathcal O_X(a+i)\,\varepsilon_I$. The differential from degree $i$ to degree $i+1$ sends the summand of $I$ to the summands of $I\cup\{j\}$, $j\notin I$, by $(-1)^{\#\{k\in I:\,k<j\}}x_j$ (exterior multiplication by $\sum_j x_j\varepsilon_j$).

proof.text:
Put $r=n+1$ and $E^i=\bigoplus_{|I|=i}\mathcal O_X(a+i)\varepsilon_I$ for $0\leq i\leq r$, and $E^i=0$ otherwise. The opens $U_k$ cover $X$: a point of Proj is a homogeneous prime not containing $S_+=(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$, so it misses some $x_k$. Each $E^i|_{U_k}$ is free with basis $b_{k,I}=e_k^{(a+i)}\varepsilon_I$, hence is a vector bundle of rank $\binom r i$. The coordinate maps in the statement glue: on $U_k\cap U_l$, the transition rule gives
$$(x_j/x_k)e_k^{(d+1)}=(x_k/x_l)^d(x_j/x_l)e_l^{(d+1)}.$$
Thus the local image of $e_k^{(d)}$ agrees with the image of $(x_k/x_l)^d e_l^{(d)}$. The coefficients commute with restriction, so these are module-sheaf morphisms. Finite matrices of these maps define the stated $\delta^i:E^i\to E^{i+1}$. This constructs exactly the requested maps, including every integer twist.

source.place: Tag 0BQS, perfect-lemma-construct-the-next-one; direct chart verification of the signed maps.

proof.text:
Write $N_I(j)=\#\{l\in I:l<j\}$. On $U_k$ put $t_j=x_j/x_k$, so $t_k=1$. Then
$$\delta b_{k,I}=\sum_{j\notin I}(-1)^{N_I(j)}t_j b_{k,I\cup\{j\}}.$$
In $\delta^2 b_{k,I}$ the term indexed by $I\cup\{j,l\}$, with $j<l$ outside $I$, occurs twice. Inserting $j$ then $l$ has sign exponent $N_I(j)+N_I(l)+1$, while inserting $l$ then $j$ has exponent $N_I(l)+N_I(j)$. Their coefficients are the same $t_jt_l=t_lt_j$, so they cancel. There are no other terms. Thus $\delta^{i+1}\delta^i=0$ on every chart and hence globally, since equality of sheaf morphisms is local by the sheaf axiom. This also holds in characteristic two, where a term plus its additive inverse is still zero.

Fix $k$. In the chart bases define $\mathcal O_{U_k}$-linear maps $h^i:E^i|_{U_k}	o E^{i-1}|_{U_k}$ by
$$h^i(b_{k,I})= egin{cases}(-1)^{N_I(k)}b_{k,I\setminus\{k\}}&k\in I,\0&k
otin I.\end{cases}$$
Take $h^0=0$ and zero maps outside the displayed degrees. These finite matrices commute with restrictions on all opens of $U_k$. We check $\delta^{i-1}h^i+h^{i+1}\delta^i=1$ on each basis element. If $k
otin I$, then $\delta h(b_{k,I})=0$ and only the $j=k$ term of $h\delta(b_{k,I})$ survives; it is $(-1)^{2N_I(k)}t_k b_{k,I}=b_{k,I}$. If $k\in I$, the $j=k$ term of $\delta h(b_{k,I})$ is again $b_{k,I}$. For each $j
otin I$, the other contribution of $\delta h$ has sign exponent $N_I(k)+N_{I\setminus\{k\}}(j)$, whereas the matching contribution of $h\delta$ has exponent $N_I(j)+N_{I\cup\{j\}}(k)$. The second exponent minus the first is $1$: use $N_{I\cup\{j\}}(k)=N_I(k)+[j<k]$ and $N_{I\setminus\{k\}}(j)=N_I(j)-[k<j]$. These two terms have the same coefficient $t_j$ and cancel. This proves the identity, including degree zero (the first case) and degree $r$ (the second case with no off-diagonal terms). The $h^i$ need only exist on this chart and are not asserted to glue.

proof.text:
Let $W\subseteq X$ be open and let $s\in E^i(W)$ satisfy $\delta^i(s)=0$. On the covering $W_k=W\cap U_k$, the identity just proved gives
$$s|_{W_k}=\delta^{i-1}\bigl(h^i(s|_{W_k})\bigr).$$
For $1\leq i\leq r$ these are the local lifts required by clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-module-exactness-local-lifting], applied to the complex $E^{i-1}\to E^i\to E^{i+1}$ on the ringed space $(X,\mathcal O_X)$. This proves exactness at every such $E^i$, including $E^r$ since $E^{r+1}=0$. At $E^0$, the same identity has $h^0=0$, so a section killed by $\delta^0$ restricts to zero on every $W_k$ and is zero by the sheaf axiom. Thus the same local-lifting criterion for $0\to E^0\to E^1$ proves exactness at $E^0$ as well. Exactness at the exterior zero terms is immediate. No exactness of global sections, flatness, regularity, or Noetherian hypothesis is used.
